thread:
support-bot: :rotating_light: Customer 'acme-markets' reported sustained latency spike for text-gen in us-west-2, started ~22:12 UTC. p95 -> 750ms, p99 ~1.4s. API errors not reported, just slow.
maya: ACK. Any recent deploys to runtime or cache layer?
jonathan: We rolled runtime v4.9.2 at 21:55 (should be fine). No infra change.
liam: Graphs: https://grafana.redwood/r/abc123/runtime-latency?orgId=1 -> big jump coincident with 21:55.
navya: Also seeing cache metrics: kv_prefix_cache miss rate spiked from ~8% to ~68% and evictions/sec jumped from ~800 -> ~12k.
sre-oncall: tagging: @sre-oncall taking this.
maya: Good catch navya. If prefix cache is thrashing, per-request token work might be skyrocketing. Can you dump cache stats and a sample stack?
navya: Dumped top keys and eviction traces. Sample: 
```
TS 1789456802 key=prefix:session:5f2a9f4a-... hits=0 inserts=120 evictions=120
TS 1789456803 key=prefix:user:1234 hits=1 inserts=1 evictions=1
total_entries=16384/16384
evictions/sec=12500
miss_rate=0.684
```
navya: Looks like a lot of unique prefixes created by session IDs being included in prefix keys.
jonathan: Wait, we changed prefix key normalization in PR #4397 earlier today to include `session_id` for better sharding. That seems suspect.
liam: Repro locally: with 50k unique session prefixes, cache fills and churns -> p95 increases similarly.
maya: So regression likely from key design change, not kernel or hardware. Any config that could mitigate quickly?
navya: Feature-flag 'prefix_cache_enabled' can be toggled per cluster. We can disable prefix caching in ~10m behind FF.
jonathan: Also can temporarily bump cache size on affected nodes (current default 16k entries). But capacity change will take time for warmup and doesn't stop new unique prefixes.
sre-oncall: Action plan: 1) Flip FF to disable prefix caching in canary -> prod 2) Hotfix PR to revert key normalization 3) Telemetry: add miss_rate alert and eviction spike alarm 4) Postmortem + tests. I can do (1).
maya: Please do (1) now. Roll to canary first.
sre-oncall: Flipping FF for canary (subset=10%): `/ops/ff toggle prefix_cache_enabled --env=us-west-2 --scope=canary`
ops-bot: Deploy started -> canary nodes updated.
navya: Canary p95 dropped from 760ms -> 240ms within 60s. miss_rate on canary down to 9%.
sre-oncall: Rolling to prod now. `/ops/ff toggle prefix_cache_enabled --env=us-west-2 --scope=prod`
ops-bot: Prod toggle complete.
liam: Prod p95 back to baseline ~230-260ms. Evictions/sec down to 600. :thumbsup:
maya: Great. For the hotfix: revert PR #4397 or at least stop including ephemeral session ids in the cache key. jonathan, can you prepare patch?
jonathan: Working on branch fix/kv-key-normalization. Patch replaces `key = f\"{prefix}:{session_id}\"` with `key = f\"{prefix}:user:{user_id}\" if user_id else f\"{prefix}:anon\"` and canonicalizes session ids out. Adding unit test.
navya: Also adding a normalization step to strip `-` and lowercase tokens for stable keys.
liam: Suggest we also add a LFU fallback or move to CLOCK to avoid massive churn when many one-off keys arrive. That will help long-tail workloads.
maya: Good idea. For now, FF flip is a safe stopgap. Next deploy after test -> canary -> prod with the key fix. Estimate 2 hrs for full QA.
sre-oncall: I'll keep alert thresholds: create alert if kv_prefix_cache.miss_rate > 0.2 for > 2m or evictions/sec > 3k for > 1m. navya can you add?
navya: On it. Creating alert: `alert: PrefixCacheThrash` expr: `sum by(cluster) (evictions_per_sec) > 3000` and `sum by(cluster) (miss_rate) > 0.2`. Also adding dashboard widget.
jonathan: Hotfix ready, PR opened: https://git.redwood/pr/4521 - includes unit tests for keys and an integration shim to run with 'session-heavy' workload.
maya: Run CI + integration on canary with patch toggled on.
liam: Also adding a deploy-time warmup: on new nodes, issue head requests for top-500 prefixes from recent 24h. That should reduce cold misses on scale-ups.
sre-oncall: Deployed change log: FF flip at 22:24; latency normalized by 22:26. Root cause: PR #4397 included session ids into prefix cache keys causing extremely high cardinality & eviction thrash.
maya: Postmortem owner? jonathan + navya pair. Add timeline, customer impact, mitigation, and corrective actions.
jonathan: Will draft postmortem. tl;dr: customer-facing slowdown for ~12 minutes for some routes in us-west-2; mitigated by FF disable; hotfix PR to revert key change pending.
navya: Follow-ups: 1) ship PR 4521 to prod 2) add unit + integration tests for cache key cardinality 3) alerting as specified 4) deploy warmup job 5) document cache key design guidelines.
sre-oncall: Any blockers?
maya: Make sure to include a checklist: don't deploy key schema changes without load test simulating high unique prefix cardinality.
liam: Also double-check any other caches using derived keys — grep for `session_id` usage in cache constructors.
jonathan: Noted. I'll run search and link findings in PR.
navya: Customer notified: support updated 'acme-markets' status and will follow up with SLA credit if requested.
maya: Thanks team. Marking thread resolved once PR is merged and alerts are in place.
ops-bot: Note: incident closed at 1789457160 UTC.
